findings.title: tenant check removed from invoice lookup
findings.explanation: GetInvoice now returns any invoice found by ID without comparing inv.TenantID to the tenantID claim. A request authenticated for tenant A can therefore read tenant B's invoice, violating tenant isolation and the required not-found behavior for foreign invoices.
findings.evidence: candidate/service.go:8-10 looks up invoices[id] and returns inv,nil; the supplied handler passes req.Claims.TenantID into GetInvoice. The previous context implementation compared inv.TenantID != tenantID before returning success. Trigger: populate an invoice with TenantID=tenant-b, then call GetInvoice(ctx, "tenant-a", id).

findings.title: destination write errors are discarded
findings.explanation: WriteBatch ignores every error returned by Destination.Put and unconditionally returns nil. When a destination fails after accepting an earlier record, Run reports a successful export even though the batch is partial, directly violating the failure contract.
findings.evidence: candidate/writer.go:5 assigns _ = dst.Put(record), and line 6 always returns nil. Context/export.go forwards Run directly to WriteBatch. Trigger: a Destination.Put implementation returns an error on the second record after accepting the first; the caller receives nil and cannot detect the partial export.

findings.title: non-ready statuses are treated as ready
findings.explanation: IsReady returns true for every status except disabled, so pending and failed resources are served. This reverses the allowlist requirement that only the exact ready status be available.
findings.evidence: candidate/status.go:3 implements status != "disabled"; Serveable delegates directly to IsReady in the supplied context. Trigger: Serveable("pending") or Serveable("failed") returns true. The changed visible test covers only ready and does not exercise the rejected states; the context explicitly identifies that gap.

summary: Correctness and integration fail because the readiness predicate admits pending and failed resources. findings.title: expiry boundary is accepted
findings.explanation: ValidAt now returns true when now equals expires because !now.After(expires) includes the equality boundary. Links must be valid strictly before expiry, so an access request at the exact expiry instant is incorrectly authorized.
findings.evidence: candidate/link.go:3 uses !now.After(expires). The supplied caller delegates Authorize directly to ValidAt and says expiry is checked on every request without rounding. Trigger: ValidAt(expires, expires) returns true; the required result is rejection.
